newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast CARB diesel down Monday with "racks".
newsitem.headline: US West Coast CARB diesel down Monday with "racks".

text.p: Spot prices for U.S. West Coast CARB diesel fuel dropped in quiet Monday session, under pressure from truck terminal markets , traders said.
"There's nothing going on the market," one trader said.
CARB diesel prices in Los Angeles were pegged 66 to 67 cents a gallon midday, a four-cent decline which traders attributed to falling "rack" prices at ARCO's terminals.
Trucks pick up diesel and other light products at terminals, or "racks," which are generally about two cents more expensive than wholesale prices at the refinery.
Traders said ARCO, along with most other refiners, had gotten through maintenance-related supply squeezes this winter and that weaker rack values reflected healthier production levels.

West Coast distillate supplies, including diesel, rose 167,000 barrels to 11.5 million barrels as of April 18, a year-on-year rise of 1.2 million barrels, according to the American Petroleum Institute.

Meanwhile, Los Angeles ultra-clean wholesale gasoline (CARB) eased one cent to 69/70 cents a gallon, weakend by a lack of interest as traders left for several industry conference in the U.S. Gulf region.
Conventional unleaded gasoline in L.A. was flat Monday.
